title: The Extraction of Marseille's old port
premise: Dominic Nakamura, a former air-crash investigator haunted by the accident that killed her family, is pulled back into the world she fled when a burner phone delivers a voice she knows is dead—her old mentor, warning of an 'accident' staged at Marseille's old port. Following the voice through a maze of shipping manifests, forged maintenance logs, and a private security firm with government ties, she uncovers a plot to sink a ferry of refugees and blame a maintenance failure, all to justify a port-security contract. The voice belongs to a colleague who faked his death to infiltrate the conspiracy, but his final act costs him everything; Dominic must choose between exposing the truth at the price of her own anonymity or letting it sink with the dead. She chooses exposure, trading her invisibility for belonging among the living.
about_author: Edmund Almeida is a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent a decade reconstructing disasters on paper before turning to fiction. He writes from a house above a working harbor, where he claims the foghorns keep his plots honest.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Insomnia, a night shift reconstructing a minor crash no one asked her to question, and a ritual visit to the memorial wall. She has built a life designed not to be noticed. Emotional beat: grief as architecture—every wall load-bearing, every window bricked.

chapters.title: The Phone That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A burner phone arrives in her mail slot with no return address. At 3 a.m. it rings: her mentor Elias Voss's voice—Elias, who died eighteen months ago. He says only: 'The old port. Count the lifeboats.' Beat: terror braided with a terrible hope.

chapters.title: Counting Lifeboats
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She researches the old port and finds the ferry Corse Libre, its lifeboat capacity quietly reduced in refit documents, its passenger manifest mostly undocumented migrants. Someone has engineered a death trap. Beat: the investigator's instinct waking like an atrophied muscle.

chapters.title: A Dead Man's Voice
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She traces the call to a relay in Genoa and realizes the voice may be synthesized—or Elias may be alive. A second call gives her a cargo container number. Beat: paranoia; she begins to distrust her own memory of the crash that made her.

chapters.title: The Man from Meridian
chapters.summary: Renan Okafor's POV. Introduce the antagonist's instrument: a Meridian Risk Solutions fixer who audits 'liabilities'—including people. He notices Dominic's inquiries into the ferry and flags her. Beat: cold, procedural menace; power as paperwork.

chapters.title: Down to the Port
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She travels to Marseille, posing as an insurance consultant, and walks the quays of the Vieux-Port. She meets Nadia, a dockworkers' union steward who owes a debt to Elias. Beat: first fragile contact with a world that might take her in.

chapters.title: Forged in the Refit
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. With Nadia's help she gets the Corse Libre's maintenance logs and finds Elias's signature—dated three weeks after his death. Beat: vertigo; the dead are signing documents, and the living are countersigning.

chapters.title: Meridian's Ledger
chapters.summary: Renan's POV. We see the conspiracy's logic from inside: a staged disaster justifies a billion-euro port-security contract, and the ferry's passengers are, in the ledger's language, 'uninsured exposure.' Beat: the banality of atrocity; corruption as accounting.

chapters.title: The Voice in the Static
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A third call: Elias, ragged, admits he faked his death to infiltrate Meridian after discovering the same pattern behind Dominic's family's crash. 'Row twelve wasn't random.' Beat: her grief recontextualized as evidence.

chapters.title: What the Crash Report Buried
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She reopens her own investigation into the crash that killed her family and finds the same forged-log signature chain. Meridian has done this before. Beat: rage replacing mourning; the price of survival was never paid by her alone.

chapters.title: Tail Lights on the Corniche
chapters.summary: Renan's POV. Meridian escalates: surveillance on Dominic, a break-in of her hotel room, a warning delivered with surgical courtesy. Renan begins to suspect Elias is alive inside his own organization. Beat: hunter becoming hunted.

chapters.title: Nadia's Debt
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Nadia reveals Elias saved her brother from a Meridian blacklisting; she chooses to help Dominic fully, wiring her into the dockworkers' network. Beat: belonging offered, and the fear of accepting it.

chapters.title: The Container
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She opens the container Elias named: inside, hard drives documenting Meridian's prior staged accidents—including hers. But Renan is waiting. She barely escapes; the drives are lost. Beat: devastating setback; she is now burned.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Elias's POV, first time. Elias, embedded as Meridian's compliance auditor, learns Renan has identified Dominic. He must choose between blowing his cover and saving her. Beat: guilt—the mentor who taught her invisibility now endangers her.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The ferry's sailing is moved up; the 'accident' is set for Thursday's fog. Dominic and Nadia plan to board as cleaners and physically prevent the sabotage—a scuttling charge in the ballast tanks. Beat: the clock becomes the antagonist.

chapters.title: The Man Who Counts
chapters.summary: Renan's POV. Renan confronts Elias with the signature discrepancy. Elias talks his way through—almost. Renan lets him go, planning to use him as bait. Beat: two predators circling, both convinced they've won.

chapters.title: Boarding the Corse Libre
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Night, fog, the ferry loading. She and Nadia reach the ballast compartment and find the charge—armed, on a timer, and a second one they didn't expect. Beat: dread made physical; the ship breathing around them.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias boards to disarm what he helped design, meets Dominic in the dark of the hull. Reunion without relief: he confesses his role in the original cover-up that let her family's crash stand. Beat: forgiveness withheld, then given—not for him, but for her.

chapters.title: The Old Port Burns
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, interleaved. The charge detonates early—Renan triggered it remotely to destroy evidence. Elias stays with the flooding compartment to hold a bulkhead open for fleeing crew. Dominic drags Nadia out. Beat: climax; sacrifice, fire, water, and the sound of the port screaming.

chapters.title: What Sank and What Surfaced
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The official story: engine failure, heroic investigation pending. But Dominic has photographed everything before the blast, and Nadia's union smuggles the archive to a journalist. Meridian's contract collapses; Renan vanishes, then is found—quietly, in Genoa. Beat: bitter, partial victory.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A public inquiry. Dominic testifies under her own name for the first time in years, telling the truth about row twelve. She is recognized, named, exposed—and survives it. Beat: the price of survival finally paid; invisibility surrendered like a weight set down.

chapters.title: The Port at Dawn
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She sleeps through the night for the first time since the crash, in a rented room above the harbor Nadia found her. The burner phone rings once—she lets it go to voicemail, then deletes it. Beat: resolution; belonging chosen, not granted, and morning arriving anyway.
